epigenetics.title: Epigenetics: The Death of the Genetic Theory of Disease Transmission

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000001.claim_text: An 1895 Journal of the American Medical Association report found the average lifespan of doctors was just 55 years.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000001.verbatim:
what he discovered, in an 1895 edition of the Journal of the American
Medical Association was that the average life of doctors was just 55 years.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000002.claim_text: The corrective action is supplementation with plant derived colloidal minerals.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000002.verbatim:
took positive
action to enhance their own lives and the lives of others by supplementing
with plant derived colloidal minerals.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000003.claim_text: Copper deficiency in humans first presents as white, gray, or silver hair.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000003.verbatim:
Copper deficiency in human beings presents itself first as white, gray, or
silver hair.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000004.claim_text: Copper is required to manufacture the heavy elastic fibers in arteries; copper deficiency causes aneurysms.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000004.verbatim:
This has got to be
due to a copper deficiency, because copper is required to manufacture the
heavy elastic fibers found in arteries.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000005.claim_text: Selenium deficiency causes infertility, miscarriages, cystic fibrosis of the pancreas, sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS), liver cirrhosis, white muscle disease, muscular dystrophy, anemia, encephalomalacia (Alzheimer's disease), cardiomyopathy, and mulberry heart disease.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000005.verbatim:
Selenium deficiency causes infertility,
miscarriages, cystic fibrosis of the pancreas, Sudden Infant Death
Syndrome in animals, liver cirrhosis, stiff lamb disease, white muscle
disease, muscular dystrophy, anemias, encephalomalacia (Alzheimer’s
disease), cardiomyopathy heart disease, and mulberry heart disease.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000006.claim_text: An early sign of selenium deficiency in older adults is the appearance of liver spots or age spots.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000006.verbatim:
Another early symptom of selenium deficiency in older humans is the
appearance of “liver spots” or “age spots.”

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000007.claim_text: Selenium supplementation prevented, and in many cases reversed or cured, selenium-deficiency diseases in animals.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000007.verbatim:
In each
case, selenium supplementation prevented the disease and in many cases
reversed or cured existing diseases, which were all significant causes of
animal losses to the livestock industry.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000008.claim_text: Zoo marmosets and shrews died of diabetes attributed to chromium and vanadium deficiency (observed at autopsy).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000008.verbatim:
I saw marmosets, alligators, and
shrews that died of diabetes, a chromium and vanadium deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000009.claim_text: Calcium deficiency alone can result in as many as 147 different diseases (osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, Bell's palsy, tinnitus, trigeminal neuralgia, spinal stenosis, and more).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000009.verbatim:
Calcium deficiency alone could result in as many as 147 different diseases
ranging from osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, osteomalacia, degenerative
arthritis, Bell’s Palsy, tinnitus, trigeminal neuralgia, and spinal stenosis to
name a few.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000010.claim_text: In the clinical phase of trace-mineral deficiency, full-blown disease states appear: cardiomyopathy, diabetes, cancer, liver cirrhosis.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000010.verbatim:
The clinical phase of trace mineral deficiencies is characterized by the onset
of full-blown disease states and even death—i.e., cardiomyopathy, diabetes,
cancer, liver cirrhosis.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000011.claim_text: The recommended maintenance dose for germanium is 20–30 mg per day (50–100 mg/day is used for serious illness requiring increased oxygenation).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000011.verbatim:
Twenty to 30 mg per day is the recommended maintenance dose for
germanium. Fifty to 100 mg per day doses are commonly used when an
individual has a serious illness that requires an increased oxygen level in
the body.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000012.claim_text: Germanium deficiency is typified by reduced immune status, arthritis, osteoporosis, low energy, and cancer.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000012.verbatim:
A severely reduced immune status, arthritis, osteoporosis, low energy, and
cancer typify deficiencies of germanium.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000013.claim_text: Humans can consume 400 mg of silver per day; silver deficiency results in an impaired immune system.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000013.verbatim:
Humans can
consume 400 mg of silver per day. A silver “deficiency” results in an
impaired immune system.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000014.claim_text: Silver is antibacterial, antiviral, and antifungal, disabling enzymes that microorganisms use for respiration.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000014.verbatim:
Silver is an anti-bacterial, anti-viral, anti-fungal, anti-metabolite that
disables specific enzymes that microorganisms use for respiration.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000015.claim_text: Per USDA researcher Richard Anderson, 90 percent of Americans are deficient in chromium.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000015.verbatim:
According to Richard Anderson, USDA, “Ninety percent of
all Americans are deficient in chromium.”

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000016.claim_text: Chromium supplementation increased laboratory-animal lifespan by 33.3 percent (Gary Evans, Bemidji State University).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000016.verbatim:
Gary Evans, Bemidji State University, Minnesota, very clearly showed an
increased life span in laboratory animals by 33.3 percent when they were
supplemented with chromium.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000017.claim_text: Chromium deficiency produces a wide range of clinical diseases (low blood sugar, type II diabetes, elevated triglycerides/cholesterol, coronary vessel disease, infertility) and a shortened lifespan, aggravated by concurrent vanadium deficiency.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000017.verbatim:
Deficiencies of chromium in humans are
characterized by a wide variety of clinical diseases as well as a shortened
life expectancy. The clinical diseases of chromium deficiency are
aggravated by concurrent vanadium deficiencies.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000018.claim_text: Cesium chloride is used in alternative cancer therapy ('high-pH therapy'), entering the cancer cell to produce an alkaline environment.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000018.verbatim:
Cesium chloride is used as part of alternative cancer therapy programs.
Cesium provides “high ph therapy” for cancer by entering the cancer cell
and producing an alkaline environment.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000019.claim_text: Pica (a compulsion to eat ice, dirt, or lead paint) is a specific sign of iron deficiency.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000019.verbatim:
Experimental evidence shows very clearly that “pica” is a specific sign of
iron deficiency. Pica can drive children and adults to eat ice (pagophagia),
dirt (geophagia), or lead paint.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000020.claim_text: Iron deficiency symptoms include fatigue, heart palpitations on exertion, reduced cognition and memory, sore tongue, and hypochromic microcytic anemia.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000020.verbatim:
Symptoms of iron deficiency
include listlessness, fatigue, heart palpitations on exertion, reduced
cognition, memory deficits, sore tongue, angular stomatitis dysphagia, and
hypochromic microcytic anemia.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000021.claim_text: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) increases iron absorption; clays and phytates decrease it.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000021.verbatim:
Ascorbic acid increases the absorption of iron;
clays and phytates decrease the absorption of iron.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000022.claim_text: Excess iron can cause liver cirrhosis, pancreatic fibrosis, diabetes, and heart failure (largely by raising the need for selenium, copper, and zinc).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000022.verbatim:
Excesses of iron can cause cirrhosis of the liver, fibrosis of the pancreas,
diabetes, and heart failure.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000023.claim_text: Iodine combines with the amino acid tyrosine to manufacture the thyroid hormone thyroxin.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000023.verbatim:
In combination with the amino acid tyrosine,
iodine is manufactured into the thyroid hormone thyroxin.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000024.claim_text: Since Americans began restricting salt intake on doctors' advice, goiter and hypothyroidism have become epidemic (iodized salt was a key iodine source).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000024.verbatim:
Iodine intake is
usually low to begin with, but since Americans have begun restricting their
salt intake at the advice of their doctors, goiter and hypothyroidism has
become epidemic.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000025.claim_text: Copper is a required cofactor to utilize iodine; copper deficiency can drive an iodine-deficiency (goiter) state even where soil iodine is adequate.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000025.verbatim:
A severe copper deficiency
in the soils of the north and the south cause the deficiency state because
copper is a required cofactor to utilize iodine.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000026.claim_text: Manganese deficiency causes birth defects (congenital ataxia, deafness), asthma, convulsions, skeletal defects, and joint problems including temporomandibular joint (jaw) disorder, repetitive motion syndrome, and carpal tunnel syndrome.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000026.verbatim:
Deficiency diseases of Mn are very striking, ranging from severe birth
defects (congenital ataxia, deafness, chondrodystrophy), asthma,
convulsions, retarded growth, skeletal defects, disruption of fat and
carbohydrate metabolism to joint problems in children and adults (i.e. TMJ,
Repetitive Motion Syndrome, Carpal Tunnel Syndrome).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000027.claim_text: Manganese is structural to the three small ear bones and to joint cartilage.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000027.verbatim:
Manganese is part of the developmental process and the structure
of the three fragile ear bones and joint cartilage.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000028.claim_text: Molybdenum is an integral part of three essential enzymes: xanthine oxidase, aldehyde oxidase, and sulfite oxidase.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000028.verbatim:
Molybdenum is known to be an integral part of no less
than three essential enzymes: Xanthine oxidase, Aldehyde oxidase, and
Sulfite oxidase.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000029.claim_text: Selenium is the most efficient antioxidant, working in the glutathione peroxidase enzyme system to keep body fats from going rancid.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000029.verbatim:
Selenium is the most efficient antioxidant (anti-peroxidant).
It’s used at the subcellular level in the glutathione peroxidase enzyme
system and metalloamino acids (selenomethionine, etc.).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000030.claim_text: High vegetable-oil intake combined with selenium deficiency is, per Wallach, the quickest route to heart attack and cancer.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000030.verbatim:
High intakes of vegetable oils,
including salad dressing and cooking oils, concurrent with a selenium
deficiency is the quickest route to a heart attack and cancer.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000031.claim_text: Tin deficiency in rats produced poor growth, hearing loss, and bilateral (male-pattern) hair loss; Wallach links tin to male-pattern baldness and hearing loss.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000031.verbatim:
Rats fed tin at 17.0 ng/gm show poor growth, reduced feeding efficiency,
hearing loss, and bilateral (male pattern) hair loss, while rats fed 1.99
|ng/gm were physiologically and anatomically normal.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000032.claim_text: Strontium deficiency is associated with certain calcium- and boron-resistant forms of osteoporosis and arthritis.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000032.verbatim:
Deficiencies of strontium are associated with certain types of Ca and boron
resistant osteoporosis and arthritis.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000033.claim_text: Strontium can substitute for calcium in many organisms, including humans, and concentrates in bone.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000033.verbatim:
where it’s most highly concentrated in mammalian bone. Strontium
can replace calcium in many organisms, including man.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000034.claim_text: Vanadium functions like insulin, making cell-membrane insulin receptors more sensitive and aiding glucose/carbohydrate intolerance.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000034.verbatim:
Vanadium appears to function
like insulin by altering cell membrane function for ion transport.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000035.claim_text: Vanadium supplementation can reduce or even eliminate most cases of adult-onset diabetes.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000035.verbatim:
Vanadium supplementation can have a major positive
economic impact by reducing or even eliminating most cases of adult onset
diabetes.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000036.claim_text: Vanadium has anticarcinogenic properties; in mice it blocked induction of mammary tumor growth and reduced tumor incidence.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000036.verbatim:
Vanadium has known
anticarcinogenic properties. Feeding 25 |ng of vanadium per gram of diet
blocked induction of mouse mammary tumor growth.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000037.claim_text: At least 70 metalloenzymes require zinc as a functional cofactor.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000037.verbatim:
There are no less than 70 metalloenzymes that require Zn as a
functional cofactor.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000038.claim_text: Zinc is integral to the RNA molecule (the 'metallic fingers') and participates in cell division and DNA synthesis.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000038.verbatim:
Zinc is also an integral part of the RNA molecule itself where Zinc
provides the “metallic fingers” and participates in cell division and
synthesis of DNA.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000039.claim_text: Zinc deficiency produces a wide range of diseases, including congenital birth defects and degenerative diseases across all age groups.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000039.verbatim:
Zinc deficiency
produces a wide range of diseases including congenital birth defects and
degenerative diseases of all age groups.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000040.claim_text: Excess dietary copper and iron, and high-phytate (vegan) diets, reduce the availability of dietary zinc.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000040.verbatim:
Excesses of dietary copper and iron and high phytate diets (vegans) will
reduce availability of dietary zinc.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000041.claim_text: Vitamin A deficiency in children causes keratitis, corneal ulcers, and blindness.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000041.verbatim:
Vitamin A deficiencies in
children caused keratitis, corneal ulcers, and blindness.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000042.claim_text: Folic acid (or zinc) deficiency causes spina bifida and serious cleft palate in infants.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000042.verbatim:
Infants born with spina bifida and serious cleft palates as a result of folic
acid or zinc deficiencies did not survive the primitive environment.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000043.claim_text: Thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency causes beriberi with resulting congestive heart failure.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000043.verbatim:
Beriberi with resultant congestive
heart failure was common, the result of a thiamin or vitamin B1 deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000044.claim_text: Vitamin B12 is a water-soluble red crystalline substance; its red color comes from the cobalt atom at its center.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000044.verbatim:
Vitamin B12 is a red crystalline substance that is water soluble. The red
color is due to the cobalt in the molecule.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000045.claim_text: About 30 percent of vitamin B12 activity is lost during cooking (electric, gas, or microwave).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000045.verbatim:
About 30 percent of B12 activity is lost during cooking
(electric, gas, or microwave).

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000046.claim_text: Supplemental chromium prevents and treats both diabetes and hypoglycemia (known since 1958).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000046.verbatim:
Since
1958, it has been known that supplemental chromium will prevent and treat
diabetes as well as hypoglycemia.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000047.claim_text: A University of Vancouver medical school statement (1985): vanadium will replace insulin for adult-onset diabetics.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000047.verbatim:
the medical school at the
University of Vancouver, BC, Canada stated that “vanadium will replace
insulin for adult onset diabetics.”

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000048.claim_text: Diabetes treatment starts with chromium and vanadium at 250 mcg/day in the initial stages to prevent insulin shock.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000048.verbatim:
Treatment of diabetes should include chromium and vanadium at 250
mcg/day in the initial stages to prevent “insulin shock”

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000049.claim_text: The diabetes regimen also includes zinc 50 mg three times daily, B-complex 50 mg three times daily (with niacin), EFAs 5 g three times daily, B12 1,000 mcg/day, quercetin 150 mg/day, copper 2-3 mg/day, lecithin 2,500 mg three times daily, and glutathione 100 mg/day.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000049.verbatim:
Treatment of diabetes should also include zinc at 50 mg t.i.d., B-complex at
50 mg t.i.d. (be sure to include niacin which is part of the GTF “glucose
tolerance factor”), essential fatty acids at 5 gm t.i.d., B12 at 1,000 mcg/day,
bioflavonoids including quercetin at 150 mg/day, copper at 2-3 mg/day,
lecithin at 2,500 mg t.i.d., and glutathione at 100 mg/day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000050.claim_text: Osteoarthritis and degenerative arthritis are a complex of nutritional deficiencies; rheumatoid arthritis's overt cause is chronic Mycoplasma infection.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000050.verbatim:
osteoarthritis and degenerative arthritis are a complex of
nutritional deficiencies. In the case of rheumatoid arthritis, a chronic
infection with a Mycoplasma spp. is the overt cause.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000051.claim_text: Arthritis treatment includes calcium at 2,000 mg/day (more if eating meat) plus magnesium at 800-1,000 mg/day.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000051.verbatim:
Treatment of arthritis should include calcium at 2000 mg/day and more if
you eat meat two or three times per day. Also take magnesium at 800-1000
mg/day

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000052.claim_text: A dietary calcium:phosphorus ratio of 2:1 is ideal but impossible to attain on an unsupplemented diet; the more meat eaten, the more calcium supplementation needed.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000052.verbatim:
A dietary calcium/phosphorus ratio of 2:1 is ideal yet impossible to attain in
an unsupplemented diet.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000053.claim_text: Asthma is a malabsorption disease featuring essential fatty acid, manganese, and magnesium deficiencies.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000053.verbatim:
Asthma is a
disease of malabsorption with essential fatty acid deficiencies and
deficiencies of manganese and magnesium.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000054.claim_text: Cor pulmonale treatment includes resolving the lung disease plus oxygen, intravenous (into a vein) hydrogen peroxide, and selenium at 500-1,000 mcg/day for adults.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000054.verbatim:
Treatment of cor pulmonale includes resolving the precipitating lung
disease and oxygen, IV hydrogen peroxide, and selenium at 500-1,000 mcg
per day for adults.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000055.claim_text: Cradle cap treatment includes regular shampooing plus B6 at 10-25 mg/day and zinc at 15-25 mg/day.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000055.verbatim:
Treatment of cradle cap includes shampooing regularly to loosen the greasy
scale, B6 at 10-25 mg per day, and zinc at 15-25 mg per day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000056.claim_text: Cancer prevention includes beta-carotene at ~300,000 International Units/day (vitamin A equivalent) and selenium at 250-500 mcg/day, alongside a low-fat, high-fiber, fried-food-free diet.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000056.verbatim:
Try to OD on beta-carotene
(almost impossible—first sign is dry skin) at about a vitamin A equivalent
of 300,000 IU per day. Use selenium at 250 to 500 mcg per day.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000057.claim_text: Per the US government, the five-year cancer survival rate has not changed in 20 years despite new surgery/radiation/chemotherapy — untreated patients as a group survived longer.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000057.verbatim:
CHEMOTHERAPY—IN FACT, UNTREATED
PATIENTS, AS A GROUP, SURVIVED LONGER!

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000058.claim_text: Osteoporosis is easy to prevent and cure with proper supplementation of stomach acid (hydrochloric acid) and calcium.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000058.verbatim:
In our personal experience
osteoporosis is easy to prevent and cure with proper supplementation of
stomach acid (HC1) and calcium.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000059.claim_text: Estrogen and fluoride supplementation alone do not solve osteoporosis.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000059.verbatim:
The big push by the “orthodox”
doctors is for estrogen and fluoride supplementation, yet these two
compounds alone do not solve the problem.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000060.claim_text: Osteoporosis treatment includes betaine hydrochloride and pancreatic enzymes (75-200 mg three times daily before meals) plus calcium and magnesium at 2,000 and 1,000 mg/day or more for the first 30 days.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000060.verbatim:
Treatment of osteoporosis should include betaine HC1 and pancreatic
enzymes at 75-200 mg t.i.d. 15 minutes before meals, and calcium and
magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day or more for the first 30 days.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000061.claim_text: Estrogen may be contraindicated for osteoporosis due to a potential carcinogenic effect — it is known to cause breast and uterine cancer.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000061.verbatim:
Estrogen may be contraindicated because of the potential carcinogenic
effect: it is known to cause breast and uterine cancer.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000062.claim_text: Per Wallach, 95 percent of all otitis (earaches) is the result of a milk allergy.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000062.verbatim: In reality, 95 percent of all otitis (earaches) is the result of a milk allergy.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000063.claim_text: The essential fatty acids are linoleic, linolenic, and arachidonic acids; about 3% of total daily calorie intake should come from EFAs (linoleic and linolenic are strictly essential).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000063.verbatim:
Three polyunsaturated fatty acids (linoleic, linolenic, and arachidonic acids)
are known as essential fatty acids (EFA). Three percent of the total daily
calorie intake is required from EFA.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000064.claim_text: EFAs are the raw material the body uses to manufacture prostaglandins, which regulate blood pressure, heart rate, vascular and bronchial dilation, blood clotting, and central nervous system (CNS) function.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000064.verbatim:
EFA’s are also the raw material for the human body to
manufacture prostaglandins that help regulate blood pressure, heart rate,
vascular dilation, blood clotting, bronchial dilation, and central nervous
system (brain and spinal cord) function.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000065.claim_text: Essential fatty acid deficiency in infants causes poor growth, eczema, and lowered resistance to infectious disease.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000065.verbatim:
EFA deficiency in human infants
results in a poor growth rate, eczema, and lowered resistance to infectious
diseases.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000066.claim_text: Wallach adds arginine, taurine, and tyrosine to the classic essential amino acids — over the long haul preventing cancer, macular degeneration, and goiter respectively.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000066.verbatim:
To the classic list of essential amino
acids, I would add arginine, taurine, and tyrosine. Over the long haul, these
three amino acids help prevent certain specific diseases. Respectively, those
diseases are cancer, macular degeneration, and goiter.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000067.claim_text: Tryptophan is a precursor of niacin and serotonin; phenylalanine of thyroxin and epinephrine; methionine forms choline and creatine phosphate.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000067.verbatim:
Tryptophan precursor of niacin and serotonin
Phenylalanine precursor of thyroxin and epinephrine
Methionine formation of choline and creatine phosphate

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000068.claim_text: Cholesterol is structural to cell walls and myelin and is the raw material for vitamin D, bile acids, and the steroid hormones (estrogen, progesterone, testosterone).
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000068.verbatim:
Cholesterol is an essential part
of the structure of cell walls, brain and spinal cord (myelin), the raw
material for the production of vitamin D in the human body, bile acids,
adrenal cortical hormones, estrogen (a cholesterol deficiency makes
menopause a living hell), progesterone, and testosterone

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000069.claim_text: Infertility is usually caused by a nutritional deficiency; Wallach reports curing several hundred cases with supplementation of vitamins, minerals, trace minerals, and digestive aids.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000069.verbatim:
INFERTILITY (curable inability to have children) is usually caused by a
nutritional deficiency of some nutrient. We have “cured” several hundred
cases of infertility by simple supplementation of vitamins, minerals, trace
minerals, and digestive aids.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000070.claim_text: Infertility protocol: EFA 5 g three times daily, L-arginine 500 mg three times daily, zinc, selenium 250 mcg/day, vitamin A 100,000 International Units/day for 30 days then 25,000 International Units/day, and germanium 50 mg/day.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000070.verbatim:
EFA at 5 gm t.i.d., 1-arginine at 500 mg t.i.d., zinc at 15 mg t.i.d., selenium
at 250 mcg/day, vitamin A at 100,000 IU/day for 30 days then drop to
25,000 IU/day, germanium at 50 mg/day

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000071.claim_text: Selenium prevents muscular dystrophy in all its forms (and Keshan disease, heart muscular dystrophy); preconception selenium levels matter for both pregnancy maintenance and muscular-dystrophy prevention.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000071.verbatim:
The selenium levels in
preconception women is important to the maintenance of pregnancy as well
as the prevention of muscular dystrophy in all of its forms

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000072.claim_text: Given selenium and vitamin E (intramuscular [injected into a muscle] or intravenous [into a vein]) at the very first onset of symptoms, muscular dystrophy can be arrested or even cured.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000072.verbatim:
If selenium and vitamin E were to
be given IM or IV at the very first onset of symptoms, the disease will be
arrested or maybe even “cured.”

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000073.claim_text: Muscular dystrophy / Keshan disease treatment uses selenium (oral colloidal, intravenous or intramuscular) at 50-1,000 mcg/day by weight plus vitamin E intramuscular at 80 mg/day.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000073.verbatim:
Treatment of MD and/or Keshan disease includes the use of selenium orally
(plant derived colloidal minerals), IV or IM at 50-1,000 mcg per day (based
on weight), vitamin E IM at 80 mg per day

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000074.claim_text: Muscle cramps (charley horse) are a mini-convulsion in the muscle resulting from deficiencies of calcium and magnesium.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000074.verbatim:
MUSCLE CRAMPS (Charley horse) are a “mini” convulsion that is taking
place in the muscle as a result of deficiencies of calcium, magnesium

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000075.claim_text: Insomnia treatment includes avoiding caffeine and food allergens, calcium (especially plant-derived colloidal), and chromium + vanadium at 25-200 mcg three times daily.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000075.verbatim:
Treatment for insomnia includes avoidance of caffeine and offending food allergens, calcium
(especially plant derived colloidal calcium), chromium and vanadium at 25-200 mcg t.i.d.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000076.claim_text: For angina, calcium 2,000 mg/day, magnesium 800 mg/day, and essential fatty acids help prevent disease progression; lifestyle change and supplementation can reverse cardiovascular disease.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000076.verbatim:
Calcium (2000 mg/day) and magnesium (800 mg/day) and essential fatty
acids can help prevent progress of current disease

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000077.claim_text: Chronic loss of the sense of smell (anosmia) is most frequently the result of a zinc deficiency.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000077.verbatim:
Chronic loss of the sense of
smell is most frequently the result of a zinc deficiency.

WAL-CLM-DDDL-000078.claim_text: Anxiety/panic treatment: avoid caffeine and sugar; chromium + vanadium 200-300 mcg/day, B6 100 mg three times daily, B3 450 mg three times daily, L-tryptophan, calcium 2,000 mg/day, magnesium 800 mg/day.
WAL-CLM-DDDL-000078.verbatim:
Take chromium and vanadium
200-300 mcg/day, B6 100 mg t.i.d., B3 450 mg t.i.d. as time-release tablets,
Bl, B2, and B5 at the rate of 50 mg t.i.d., L-tryptophan 10 grams t.i.d.,
calcium 2000 mg/day, and magnesium at 800 mg/day.

consumption contributes to the prevention and repair of spider veins, varicose
veins, hemorrhoids, and aneurysms.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000052.claim_text: Methionine is a sulfur-containing amino acid whose derivative S-adenosyl methionine serves as the body's main methyl donor, and it is an intermediate in the biosynthesis of cysteine, carnitine, taurine, lecithin, and phosphatidylcholine. Wallach reports that laboratory rats fed a methionine-free diet developed steatohepatitis (fatty liver disease), anemia, and lost two-thirds of their body weight over five weeks -- all of which were resolved by methionine supplementation. In his words: 'Laboratory rats fed a methionine-free diet developed steatohepatitis (fatty liver disease), anemia, and lost two thirds of their body weight over five weeks. Supplementation with methionine resolved all of the disease problems of the study group.'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000052.verbatim:
Laboratory rats fed a methionine-free diet developed steatohepatitis (fatty
liver disease), anemia, and lost two thirds of their body weight over five weeks.
Supplementation with methionine resolved all of the disease problems of the
study group.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000053.claim_text: Phenylalanine is a precursor for tyrosine and, through it, the signaling molecules dopamine, norepinephrine (noradrenaline), and epinephrine (adrenaline), plus the skin and hair pigment melanin (which requires a copper cofactor). Wallach explains that the inborn error phenylketonuria -- the inability to metabolize phenylalanine, which he says is falsely believed to be genetically transmitted -- is managed by avoiding phenylalanine (including the sweetener aspartame), and that the DL-phenylalanine form is marketed as a sleep aid, antidepressant, and analgesic (pain reliever). In his words: 'Phenylalanine is a precursor for tyrosine, the monoamine signaling molecules dopamine, norepinephrine (noradrenaline), and epinephrine (adrenaline), and the skin and hair pigment melanin (this procedure requires the cofactor copper).'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000053.verbatim:
Phenylalanine is a precursor for tyrosine, the monoamine signaling molecules
dopamine, norepinephrine (noradrenaline), and epinephrine (adrenaline), and the
skin and hair pigment melanin (this procedure requires the cofactor copper).

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000054.claim_text: Taurine -- a sulfonic-acid amino acid that conjugates bile acids, acts as an antioxidant, and modulates calcium signaling -- is essential to the cardiovascular system, skeletal muscle, the retina, and the central nervous system. Wallach states that taurine is required for the maintenance of skeletal muscle and healthy blood pressure, and that taurine deficiency can produce cataracts and retinal damage; he also notes that doses above 2 grams per day have been shown to contribute to psoriasis. In his words: 'Taurine is required for the maintenance of skeletal muscle and the maintenance of healthy blood pressure. Taurine deficiency can produce cataracts and retinal damage.'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000054.verbatim:
Taurine is required for the maintenance of skeletal muscle and the
maintenance of healthy blood pressure. Taurine deficiency can produce cataracts
and retinal damage.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000055.claim_text: Threonine is a polar amino acid that, together with serine, is one of only two protein-building amino acids bearing an alcohol group, making it a site for post-translational modification (glycosylation and phosphorylation by threonine kinase). Wallach notes threonine is converted to pyruvate via threonine dehydrogenase, and through intermediates can yield acetyl coenzyme A and glycine or alpha-ketobutyrate feeding into the succinyl-coenzyme A pathway. In his words: 'Threonine (Thr) is an alpha amino acid that is classified as polar; its codons are ACU, ACA, ACC, and ACG. Together with serine, threonine is one of only two proteinogenic amino acids that bear an alcohol group.'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000055.verbatim:
Threonine (Thr) is an alpha amino acid that is classified as polar; its codons
are ACU, ACA, ACC, and ACG. Together with serine, threonine is one of only
two proteinogenic amino acids that bear an alcohol group.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000056.claim_text: Tryptophan is the biochemical precursor of the neurotransmitter serotonin (which can be converted to the sleep hormone melatonin), and niacin is also synthesized from it. Wallach explains that fructose malabsorption, lactose intolerance, and gluten intolerance reduce tryptophan absorption from the intestine, lowering blood tryptophan and producing clinical depression, and that tryptophan supplements are sold as sleep aids while its metabolite 5-hydroxytryptophan has been suggested for seizure disorders and depression. In his words: 'The disorders, fructose malabsorption, lactose intolerance, and gluten intolerance cause a reduced state of tryptophan absorption from the intestine, therefore causing reduced levels of tryptophan in the blood and clinical depression. Tryptophan supplements are sold as sleep aids.'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000056.verbatim:
The disorders, fructose malabsorption, lactose intolerance, and gluten
intolerance cause a reduced state of tryptophan absorption from the intestine,
therefore causing reduced levels of tryptophan in the blood and clinical
depression. Tryptophan supplements are sold as sleep aids.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000057.claim_text: Tyrosine is a precursor for the neurotransmitters dopamine and norepinephrine and serves in cellular signal transduction (as a receiver of phosphate groups via protein kinases). Wallach reports that several studies show tyrosine to be of benefit for colds, stress, fatigue, the loss of a loved one or divorce, prolonged work hours, and sleep deprivation -- reducing stress-hormone levels and stress-related weight loss and improving cognitive and physical performance -- though because tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting enzyme its effects are less than those of L-Dopa. In his words: 'Tyrosine is a precursor for the synthesis of neurotransmitters, and particularly for dopamine and norepinephrine. Several studies have shown tyrosine to be of benefit for colds, stress, fatigue, loss of a loved one or divorce, prolonged work hours, and sleep deprivation, with reductions of stress hormone levels...'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000057.verbatim:
Tyrosine is a precursor for the synthesis of neurotransmitters, and particularly
for dopamine and norepinephrine. Several studies have shown tyrosine to be of
benefit for colds, stress, fatigue, loss of a loved one or divorce, prolonged work
hours, and sleep deprivation, with reductions of stress hormone levels

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000058.claim_text: Valine is a branched-chain amino acid (named for the plant valerian) that functions in the nervous system to support cognitive function, and in the building and maintenance of muscle, muscle-tissue recovery and metabolism after exercise, and increased exercise endurance. Wallach notes that in sickle-cell disease valine substitutes for the water-loving amino acid glutamic acid in hemoglobin; because valine is water-repelling (hydrophobic), the hemoglobin is then more likely to aggregate. In his words: 'It functions in the nervous system to support cognitive function, function and maintenance of muscle, and the muscle tissue recovery and metabolism post-exercise and for increasing exercise endurance.'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000058.verbatim:
It functions in the nervous
system to support cognitive function, function and maintenance of muscle, and
the muscle tissue recovery and metabolism post-exercise and for increasing
exercise endurance.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000059.claim_text: The two classically essential fatty acids -- alpha-linolenic acid (an omega-3) and linoleic acid (an omega-6) -- cannot be synthesized and must be consumed daily, in proper omega-3 to omega-6 ratio, to make eicosanoids, endocannabinoids, and other signaling molecules and to regulate inflammation. Wallach states that essential fatty acid deficiency produces thrombosis (cerebral stroke, coronary thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and deep vein thrombosis), skin disease (dry/cracked skin, dermatitis, eczema, psoriasis, rosacea, acne), respiratory disease (asthma, chronic bronchitis, unremitting cough), and depression -- and that low omega-3 (docosahexaenoic acid) is associated with increased depression and suicide. In his words: 'Essential fatty acid deficiencies will produce thrombosis (i.e., cerebral stroke, coronary thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and deep vein thrombosis), skin disease (including dry/cracked skin, dermatitis, eczema, psoriasis, rosacea acnea, etc,), respiratory disease (including asthma, chonic bronchitis, unremitting cough, etc,), and depression.'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000059.verbatim:
Essential fatty acid deficiencies will produce thrombosis (i.e., cerebral stroke,
coronary thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and deep vein thrombosis), skin
disease (including dry/cracked skin, dermatitis, eczema, psoriasis, rosacea acnea,
etc,), respiratory disease (including asthma, chonic bronchitis, unremitting cough,
etc,), and depression.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000060.claim_text: Wallach describes three basic forms of minerals and their very different bioavailability. Metallic minerals (eggshell, oyster shell, calcium carbonate, dolomite, antacids such as Rolaids and Tums, and the gluconate/carbonate/oxide forms in most tablets) are, despite claims to the contrary, only 8 to 12 percent absorbable by humans -- dropping to roughly 3 to 5 percent after age 35 to 40. Chelated minerals (created by the livestock industry in the 1960s, the mineral wrapped in an amino acid such as EDTA) absorb better, and colloidal minerals -- ultra-fine plant-derived particles suspended in liquid -- are the most usable, which is why he calls plant-derived colloidal minerals the most critical of the 90 essential nutrients. In his words: 'Metallic minerals, despite wild claims to the contrary, are only eight percent to twelve percent biologically available to all vertebrates, including humans; after attaining the age of 35 to 40 years the absorptive availability to humans is reduced to somewhere around three to five percent.'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000060.verbatim:
Metallic minerals, despite wild claims to the contrary, are only eight percent
to twelve percent biologically available to all vertebrates, including humans; after
attaining the age of 35 to 40 years the absorptive availability to humans is


reduced to somewhere around three to five percent.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000061.claim_text: Calcium is the most abundant mineral in the body, with about 99% in the bones and teeth (as hydroxyapatite) and the rest used as a cofactor for blood clotting, muscle contraction, and the heart's electrical conduction. Wallach states that, contrary to the medical belief that high calcium causes kidney stones, a high dietary calcium intake actually reduces the risk of nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, and kidney stones, and that no fewer than 147 deficiency diseases are attributed to calcium deficiency or imbalance. His Common Calcium-Deficiency Diseases include: osteoporosis (with kyphosis, scoliosis, Dowager's hump, lordosis, spontaneous fractures), receding gums, osteomalacia, myelosclerosis, arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, bone spurs, kidney stones, nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism, hypertension, insomnia, calcium deposits (vascular, restless leg, atrial fibrillation), cramps and twitches (Tourette's syndrome), premenstrual syndrome, low-back pain (sciatica), neuropathy (Bell's palsy, trigeminal neuralgia), tetany with convulsions, and panic attacks. In his words: 'There are no less than 147 different deficiency-diseases that are directly attributed to a calcium deficiency or imbalance.'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000061.verbatim:
Calcium deposits (vascular, tendons, ligaments, restless leg, atrial-fibrillation, etc.) : Same as osteoporosis

Cramps & twitches (Tourette's syndrome, foot, calf, hamstring, eyelids, etc.) : Same as osteoporosis

PMS (emotional & physical symptoms) : Same as osteoporosis

Low back (sciatica, spasm, disc, etc.) : Same as osteoporosis

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000062.claim_text: Chromium activates the glucose tolerance factor and is essential to insulin function and blood-sugar control; Wallach notes a USDA spokesperson stated 90% of Americans are deficient, that dietary sugar loads raise urinary chromium loss by 300% for 12 hours, and that chromium-supplemented animals lived 33% longer. Chromium-deficiency diseases (aggravated by concurrent vanadium deficiency and dietary sugar) include: low blood sugar, reactive hypoglycemia, bed-wetting, pre-diabetes, type-2 diabetes, hyperinsulinemia, hyperactivity, learning disability, attention deficit disorder (ADD/ADHD), hyperirritability, depression, manic depression (bipolar disorder), 'Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde' rages, impaired growth, peripheral neuropathy, negative nitrogen balance (protein/muscle loss), elevated triglycerides (over 200) and cholesterol (over 270), coronary artery disease, aortic cholesterol plaque, infertility (anovulation and low sperm count), and a shortened lifespan. In his words: 'Diseases and Symptoms of Chromium Deficiency: Low blood sugar; Reactive hypoglycemia; Bed wetting; Pre-diabetes; Diabetes (Type 2); Hyperinsulinemia; Hyperactivity; Learning disability; ADD/ADHD.'

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000063.claim_text: Copper is a universally important cofactor for hundreds of metalloenzymes -- required for the pigment melanin (hair and skin color), for lysyl oxidase that gives blood vessels, skin, and discs their tensile strength, and for oxygen handling in respiration; Wallach calls copper deficiency widespread and notes it underlies several diseases the medical community wrongly blames on prions or infection. Copper-deficiency diseases include: white/gray/silver and dry brittle hair, ptosis (sagging eyelids, skin, breasts, belly), hernias, varicose and spider veins (hemorrhoids), aneurysms, Kawasaki disease, Marfan's syndrome, anemia, hypo- and hyperthyroid, arthritis, ruptured and bulging discs, liver cirrhosis, violent/blind-rage/explosive/criminal behavior, learning disabilities, cerebral palsy with cerebellar hypoplasia (congenital ataxia), high cholesterol, iron-storage disease, reduced glucose tolerance (hypoglycemia, reactive hypoglycemia), and neutropenia. In his words: 'Diseases and Symptoms of Copper Deficiency: White hair, gray hair, silver hair; Dry brittle hair ("steely wool" in sheep); Enzootic ataxia in sheep; Mad cow disease (BSE cattle); Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (BSE in humans); Ptosis (ie., sagging tissue -- eye lids, skin, breasts, belly, etc.); Hernias (congenital and acquired); Varicose veins/ spider veins (hemorrhoids); Aneurysms (aortic, cerebral, coronary, gastric, etc.).'
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000063.verbatim:
Ptosis (ie., sagging tissue—eye lids, skin, breasts, belly, etc.)
Hernias (congenital and acquired)

Varicose veins/ spider veins (hemorrhoids)

Marfan's syndrome

Liver cirrhosis

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000064.claim_text: Wallach reports that although silver is not required by any known biological system, many researchers consider it an essential element for its role as a systemic disinfectant and immune-system support. He cites it as a broad-spectrum antibacterial, antiviral, and antifungal agent that disables the enzymes microbes use for respiration, notes that humans can safely consume 400 milligrams of silver per day, and states that a silver 'deficiency' results in an impaired immune system with a higher rate of illness such as colds and influenza. Drawing on Dr. Robert Becker's The Body Electric, he adds that silver also stimulates the growth and repair of injured tissue.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000064.verbatim:
A silver “deficiency”
results in an impaired immune system. In the Body Electric Dr. Robert Becker
identified a relationship between low levels of tissue and dietary silver and the
rate of illness (such as flu, colds, etc.)

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000065.claim_text: Wallach identifies aluminum's known biological function as activating the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase and increasing newborn survival, and reports that Professor Gerhard Schrauzer (former chair of chemistry at the University of California, San Diego) argues it should be classed as an essential mineral for all vertebrates including humans. He stresses that aluminum is remarkably nontoxic at dietary levels -- far less toxic than heavy metals -- and that it competes with calcium absorption, so excess can reduce skeletal mineralization. He explicitly rejects the popular fear that aluminum causes Alzheimer's disease, citing the 1992 Oxford study (Frank Watt and colleagues, in Nature) that found identical brain-aluminum levels in Alzheimer's patients and controls, and the Alzheimer's Society's 2013 position that no causal link has been demonstrated.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000065.verbatim:
The known biological function of aluminum is to activate the enzyme succinic
dehydrogenase; it increases the survival rate of the newborn

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000066.claim_text: Wallach presents arsenic as an essential trace element -- required for survivability of the newborn and for neonatal growth -- not merely the notorious poison of popular reputation. He notes arsenic promotes growth in chicks and tadpoles, that in combination with choline it prevents perosis ('slipped tendon') in poultry, and that its role in human physiology lies in methyl-group metabolism and polyamine synthesis. He distinguishes organically-bound arsenic, which is far safer, from metallic arsenic, which is about 65 times more toxic, and recounts that low-dose arsenic trioxide is an approved, effective therapy for acute promyelocytic leukemia, a blood and bone-marrow cancer, with 'Fowler's solution' historically used for psoriasis.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000066.verbatim:
Arsenic promotes the growth rate of chicks at 90 to 120 ppm. The rate of
growth and metamorphosis of tadpoles is enhanced by the presence of arsenic.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000067.claim_text: Wallach explains that elemental gold is biologically inert -- tasteless, unabsorbed, and passed unchanged in the feces with no nutritional value -- so the gold leaf in gourmet foods and liqueurs is purely decorative. Gold compounds (gold sodium thiomalate, aurothioglucose), by contrast, are given by conventional physicians as an add-on anti-inflammatory for rheumatoid arthritis: effective against active joint inflammation but not for advanced destructive disease, and anti-inflammatory rather than pain-relieving. He notes the standard intramuscular schedule (10 milligrams rising to 50 milligrams weekly to a one-gram total), warns it is contraindicated in liver, kidney, and blood disease and in lupus, and lists toxic reactions including itching, dermatitis, mouth inflammation, gastrointestinal upset, blood in the urine, aplastic anemia, and hepatitis.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000067.verbatim:
Gold has been reported only to be effective against active joint
inflammation and is not usually helpful for advanced destructive rheumatoid
arthritis,

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000068.claim_text: Wallach classifies boron as an essential mineral for bone metabolism -- needed for the efficient use of calcium and magnesium and for the proper functioning of the ovaries, testes, and adrenal glands. He notes boron was only universally accepted as essential for humans around 1990, and that within eight days of boron supplementation women lost 40 percent less calcium, 33 percent less magnesium, and less phosphorus through their urine, while blood estradiol and testosterone in both men and women nearly doubled -- to levels comparable with estrogen-replacement therapy. He frames boron as central to maintaining bone and normal sex-hormone levels.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000068.verbatim:
Boron is essential for bone metabolism, including the efficient use of calcium
and magnesium and for the proper functioning of the ovaries, testes

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000069.claim_text: Wallach notes that barium's essentiality in mammals was established in 1949 (Rygh). Most naturally-occurring barium minerals (barite, witherite) are water-insoluble, and barium sulfate has very low toxicity together with high X-ray opacity -- which is why it serves as the contrast medium (the 'barium meal' and 'barium enema') for upper and lower gastrointestinal X-ray studies of the digestive system.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000069.verbatim:
Barium sulfate has a very low toxicity and relatively high density and has
a high opacity to X-rays. It is used as a contrast media in X-ray imaging of
the digestive system

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000070.claim_text: Although beryllium appears on Wallach's list of essential minerals, the stance he records here is a safety caution: pure powdered beryllium and its compounds must be handled with care because of the risk of acute beryllium disease or chemical pneumonitis (first reported in Europe in 1933 and in the United States in 1943), and chronic berylliosis resembles pulmonary sarcoidosis.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000070.verbatim:
Pure powdered beryllium and its compounds should be handled with care
because of the potential for acute beryllium disease or chemical pneumonitis

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000071.claim_text: Wallach notes that bismuth (chemically resembling arsenic and antimony) is not on the essential-mineral list but has clear medicinal use: bismuth subsalicylate is the antidiarrheal active ingredient in 'Pink Bismuth' products such as Pepto-Bismol and the reformulated Kaopectate. He recounts that a combination of bismuth subsalicylate, bismuth subcitrate, and the antibiotic tetracycline -- used in pigs since 1952 -- was approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration in 1994 to cure human gastric ulcers, underscoring his point that the bacterium Helicobacter pylori, not stress, causes most stomach and peptic ulcers (the 1983 Marshall-Warren discovery).
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000071.verbatim:
Bismuth subsalicylate is used as an antidiarrheal; it is the active ingredient
in “Pink Bismuth” compounds such as Pepto-Bismol

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000072.claim_text: Wallach describes bromine as a halogen related to iodine, fluorine, and chlorine. Bromine compounds such as potassium bromide were used as sedatives through the 19th and 20th centuries, until the United States Food and Drug Administration pulled over-the-counter bromide sedatives such as Bromo-Seltzer from sale in 1975, and he notes that toxic reactions from a bromine overdose can resemble acne-like skin eruptions.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000072.verbatim:
Bromine compounds, such as potassium bromide, were used as sedatives in
the 19th and 20th centuries.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000073.claim_text: Wallach notes that carbon -- one of the few elements known since antiquity -- functions as the essential structural atom for all organic molecules, including the genes themselves, and is present at very high concentrations in living tissue (around 454,000 parts per million in land plants and 465,000 in land animals, with roughly 280,000 in bone).
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000073.verbatim:
Carbon
functions as an essential structural atom for all organic molecules

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000074.claim_text: Wallach notes that cadmium -- a soft metal chemically similar to zinc, best known as a kidney-accumulating heavy metal -- nonetheless has biological functions: it can substitute for zinc in zinc-deficiency states by activating some zinc-dependent enzymes (such as carbonic anhydrase in marine diatoms), it stimulates the hatching of nematode (worm) cysts, and cadmium-bound proteins have been isolated from molluscs and horse kidney. He adds the historical note that the 1907 British Pharmaceutical Codex listed cadmium iodide as a therapy for enlarged joints, scrofulous (tuberculous) glands, and chilblains.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000074.verbatim:
Cadmium can substitute for zinc in zinc deficiency states by its ability
to activate some zinc dependent enzymes

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000075.claim_text: Wallach describes cerium -- the most abundant of the rare-earth elements -- as able to function in a manner similar to calcium in all organisms: it is deposited in bone and has been shown to stimulate metabolism. He notes cerium nitrate is used as a topical disinfectant for severe burn victims.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000075.verbatim:
Cerium can function in a similar fashion to calcium an all organisms, so it is
deposited in bones and has been shown to stimulate metabolism.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000076.claim_text: Wallach presents chlorine (as chloride) as essential to all living organisms for electrochemical and catalytic functions: it activates numerous enzymes and is the basic raw material the stomach's gastric 'chief' cells use to manufacture hydrochloric acid -- which keeps the stomach sterile, boosts the protein-digesting enzyme pepsin, and improves absorption of minerals and vitamin B12 (via intrinsic factor). Salt (sodium chloride) is the universal source of chloride ions. He also recounts chlorine's public-health legacy: Labarraque's chlorinated-lime solutions and Semmelweis's 1847 chlorine hand-disinfection that ended the spread of childbed fever, and the 1918 mandate to chlorinate United States drinking water.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000076.verbatim:
Essential for all living organisms and electrochemical and catalytic functions,
activates numerous enzymes and is the basic raw material for the gastric “chief”
cells to manufacture HCl for stomach acidity

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000077.claim_text: Cobalt is essential because it is the metal at the center of vitamin B12 (cobalamin): a single cobalt atom sits in B12's tetrapyrrole ring, and the vitamin acts as a cofactor for transferring methyl groups -- with folic acid, choline, and methionine -- to build RNA and DNA, and for myelin formation and red-blood-cell synthesis. Wallach recounts that cobalt's essentiality was discovered when veterinarians found the fatal 'bush sickness' in Australian and New Zealand livestock (emaciation, listlessness, anorexia, microcytic anemia) could be cured by cobalt supplementation, and that pernicious anemia and demyelination of the spinal cord are the classic signs of B12/cobalt deficiency in humans -- common in vegans, after stomach or ileum surgery, and with hypochlorhydria (low stomach acid). He prefers 250 to 400 micrograms a day (above the 3-to-4 microgram conventional allowance), notes calcium is required for B12 to cross the intestinal wall, and warns that cobalt excess (20 to 30 milligrams a day) can drive erythropoiesis; cobalt is also a cofactor for thyroid-hormone production.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000077.verbatim:
parasites (tapeworm), celiac disease, gluten intolerance, and other malabsorption
diseases. Pernicious anemia

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000078.claim_text: Wallach notes that cesium is an alkaline mineral that behaves chemically like sodium, potassium, and rubidium, entering an ion-exchange complex with potassium (so extra dietary potassium speeds cesium's excretion). He records its use as a cancer treatment: cesium chloride is used as part of alternative cancer therapy, providing 'high pH therapy' by entering the cancer cell and producing an alkaline environment, and has been recommended for cancers including sarcomas, bronchiogenic carcinoma, and colon cancer.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000078.verbatim:
Cesium chloride is used as part of alternative cancer therapy. Cesium provides
“high pH therapy for cancer by entering the cancer cell and producing an alkaline
environment.” Cesium has been recommended for the treatment of many types
of cancer including sarcomas, bronchiogenic carcinoma, and colon cancer

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000079.claim_text: In Epigenetics, Wallach's entry for dysprosium -- a rare-earth metal -- covers only its natural distribution (parts-per-million across igneous rocks, shale, sandstone and limestone, with animal concentrations highest in bone) and its discovery history; he assigns it no specific human deficiency disease or nutritional function here. This reflects how little is individually established about the rare-earth trace minerals, which Wallach groups broadly as life-supporting elements while saying little element-by-element. Dysprosium was named in 1886 by the French chemist Paul Emile Lecoq de Boisbaudran from the Greek 'dysprositos', meaning 'hard to get', and is never found free in nature.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000079.verbatim:
Dysprosium was first identified in 1886 by a French chemist, Paul Emile Lecoq
de Boisbaudran while he was studying holmium oxide. He gave it the name
dysprosium from the Greek word dysprositos meaning “hard to get,”

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000080.claim_text: Wallach's Epigenetics entry for erbium -- a rare-earth metal -- records only its natural distribution (parts-per-million in rocks, plants and animals, concentrating in bone) and its discovery, plus that a large variety of medical applications in dermatology and dentistry use erbium; he assigns it no specific human nutritional deficiency or function. Erbium was discovered in 1843 by Carl Gustaf Mosander, who split 'yttria' from the mineral gadolinite into three fractions -- yttria, erbia and terbia -- and its oxide has a distinctive pink color. It is one of the individually under-studied rare-earth trace elements in his framework.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000080.verbatim:
Erbium (for Ytterby, a village in Sweden) was discovered by Carl Gustaf
Mosander in 1843. Mosander separated “yttria” from the mineral gadolinite into
three fractions which he called yttria, erbia, and terbia.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000081.claim_text: Wallach's stance on europium -- a 'light' rare-earth metal -- is part of his broader thesis that rare-earth trace minerals support longevity: europium extended the lifespan of a laboratory species (the protozoan Tetrahymena pyriformis) by 100 percent over its normal expected lifespan. He also notes europium is found in higher concentrations in the breast milk of women in third-world countries than in American women. As with the other rare earths, he offers little element-specific detail beyond this life-extension observation and its natural distribution.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000081.verbatim:
Europium has extended the life of laboratory species (e.g., Tetrahymena
pyriformis) over their normal expected lifespan by 100%. Europium is found in
higher concentrations in breast milk from women in third world countries than in
American women.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000082.claim_text: Wallach holds a dual stance on fluorine/fluoride. On one hand he accepts it as an essential trace mineral: prior to 1972 fluoride was thought essential only for warding off dental caries (cavities) via tooth enamel, and in 1972 the researcher Schwarz proved fluoride to be a genuine essential mineral. On the other hand he treats water fluoridation as highly controversial and links it to cancer. Following 1977 epidemiological studies by Yiamouyiannis and Burk, full-scale congressional hearings examined the charge that 10,000 excess cancer deaths were caused by fluoridating certain public water systems. The resulting U.S. National Toxicology Program animal study, reported in 1990, found increased precancerous lesions and squamous-cell carcinoma of the oral mucous membranes, a rare osteosarcoma (bone cancer) at double the rate in males as females, and a significant increase in thyroid follicular-cell tumors and liver cancer. Clinical fluoride toxicity appears as dental fluorosis at 2 to 7 parts-per-million and osteosclerosis at 8 to 20 parts-per-million, with chronic systemic toxicity at 20 to 80 milligrams per day over years; the average American already takes in about 4.4 milligrams per day from food, toothpaste, supplements and water.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000082.verbatim:
In 1990 the results of the fluoride study showed an increase in rat
precancerous lesions in the oral mucus membrane cells; there was an increase
in cancers of the oral mucus membranes (squamous cell carcinoma); a rare
form of osteosarcoma appeared at double the rate in males as females;

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000083.claim_text: Iron is an essential mineral; a healthy adult carries 3 to 5 grams, most of it in hemoglobin and myoglobin, where iron carries oxygen (iron is to hemoglobin what magnesium is to chlorophyll). Wallach stresses that pica -- obsessive cravings driving children and adults to eat ice (pagophagia), dirt (geophagia), lead-paint chips and high-calorie snack foods -- is a specific sign of iron deficiency, and that the snack-food form can cause weight gain and obesity. Iron deficiency arises from unsupplemented pregnancy, menstruation, chronic infection, hypochlorhydria (low stomach acid from salt-restricted diets or proton-pump inhibitors), chronic diarrhea, chronic bleeding, and impaired absorption from high-fat, high-phytate or gluten diets. Its symptoms include listlessness, fatigue, heart palpitations on exertion, rapid pulse (tachycardia), reduced cognition and memory, sore tongue, difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and hypochromic microcytic anemia. Stomach hydrochloric acid and vitamin C aid absorption; heme iron from meat is about 10 percent absorbable versus 1 percent from plants (phytates bind it). He notes excess iron storage is usually caused by deficiencies of selenium, copper or zinc and is falsely blamed for liver cirrhosis, pancreatic fibrosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and diabetes.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000083.verbatim:
tongue, angular stomatitis, dysphagia (pica), hypochromic microcytic anemia,
weight gain, obesity, etc.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000084.claim_text: Wallach's stance on gallium -- a trace element claimed to be essential in 1938 and again in 1958 -- centers on the brain and brain cancer. He states gallium has specific areas of metalloenzyme activity in the human brain and has been reported to specifically reduce the rate of brain cancer in laboratory animals, and that British research shows supplementing the diets of pregnant women will reduce the rate of brain cancer in their children. Gallium maltolate, an orally absorbable form of the gallium ion, is used in medical treatments for brain cancer, inflammation and certain infectious diseases. Because gallium and ferric (iron) salts behave similarly in biological systems, gallium ions often mimic iron ions in medical applications.
WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000084.verbatim:
Gallium was claimed to be essential in 1938 and again in 1958. Gallium
has specific areas of metalloenzyme activity in the human brain and has been
reported to specifically reduce the rate of brain cancer in laboratory animals.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000086.claim_text: Germanium is an essential trace mineral that Wallach describes as a highly efficient intracellular electrical-impulse initiator and a metallic cofactor for oxygen utilization, closely related to silica and carbon. He recounts that Dr. Kazuhiko Asai found germanium in fossilized plant life and in healing herbs (garlic, aloe, comfrey, chlorella, ginseng, watercress, Shiitake mushroom and others), which accumulate it at 100 to 2,000 parts-per-million, and that the 'holy waters' at Lourdes contain large amounts of germanium and lithium. Germanium enhances the immune system by stimulating natural killer cells, interferon, macrophages and T-suppressor cells, and Russian researchers attributed anti-cancer activity to it. Asai synthesized the organic form GE-132 (carboxyethyl germanium sesquioxide) in 1967, which is absorbed at about 30 percent efficiency. Wallach states that germanium deficiency is typified by severely reduced immune status, arthritis, osteoarthritis, low energy and cancer; the maintenance dose is 20 to 30 milligrams per day, rising to 50 to 100 milligrams per day for serious illness requiring increased body oxygen.

Deficiencies of germanium are typified by a severely reduced immune status,

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000087.claim_text: Hydrogen is an essential structural element: it is the major constituent of water (about 70 percent of the human body is water) and of all organic molecules, and Wallach frames the body's acid-base balance as, in fact, the regulation of hydrogen-ion (H+) levels in cellular and extracellular fluids. Healthy blood pH ranges from 7.36 to 7.44; below 7.30 is acidosis and above 7.44 is alkalosis, while values below 6.8 or above 7.8 are rapidly fatal. The body controls hydrogen-ion concentration by dilution, buffering (reacting in fractions of a second), respiration (minutes) and the kidney (up to hours or days). Large amounts of hydrogen ions are generated or retained in disease states such as emphysema, diabetes, anxiety, chloride loss, cystic fibrosis and Addison's disease. He notes a practical corollary: bladder infections (cystitis) can often be controlled by acidifying the urine with unsweetened cranberry juice.

Hydrogen functions as a major constituent of water (70% of the human body

human body is in fact the regulation of the hydrogen ion (H+) levels of cellular
and extracellular fluids.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000091.claim_text: Mercury occurs universally in living things and is a well-known toxic element; Wallach traces its accumulation to industry, mining, agriculture, dental amalgam fillings, and micro-organisms that convert it to methyl mercury in aquatic sediments. Methyl mercury (the form in fish) crosses the placenta easily and has a biological half-life of about 70 days; heavy fish eaters, especially of large predators such as shark, tuna and swordfish, can reach tissue levels up to 400 micrograms per kilogram. Direct mercury poisoning is primarily neurological -- tremors, vertigo, irritability, moodiness, depression, salivation, inflammation of the mouth (stomatitis) and diarrhea -- while poisoning with the more toxic alkyl mercury progresses to loss of coordination, vision and hearing. Wallach notes selenium and mercury are mutually antagonistic: selenium protects the kidney from mercury-induced tissue death (necrosis) and limits placental transfer. He cites the 1962 Minamata Bay disaster in Japan and a mass poisoning in Iran (bread from mercury-treated seed grain) as producing congenital brain defects, cerebral palsy and infant deaths, and relays the theory that dental-amalgam vapor is linked to multiple sclerosis, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, Lou Gehrig's disease) and Parkinson's disease.

inflammation of the mouth [stomatitis] and diarrhea).

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000093.claim_text: Iodine is an essential mineral concentrated in the thyroid gland; combined with the amino acid tyrosine it is manufactured into the thyroid hormone thyroxin, which regulates digestion, heart rate, body temperature, sweat-gland activity, the nervous and reproductive systems, general metabolism and body weight. Wallach argues iodine intake is usually low to begin with, and that as Americans restrict their salt intake on medical advice, physician-caused goiter and hypothyroidism have become epidemic; copper is a required cofactor for using iodine, so copper-poor soils also drive goiter. Low iodine and thyroid function produce hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's disease) -- fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, hair loss, depression, constipation, dry skin, poor memory, goiter, infertility, and congenital birth defects (cretinism in the newborn). He notes many foods act as goitrogens that interfere with thyroid function (dietary and waterborne nitrates, cruciferous vegetables, gluten intolerance) and that about 11 million Americans have an under- or over-active thyroid; the average American takes in only 170 to 250 micrograms of iodine per day, and metallic iodine is not toxic up to 2,000 micrograms per day.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000094.claim_text: Potassium is essential to all organisms and is the major positively-charged ion (cation) inside cells, driving electrochemical and enzyme functions; it makes up about five percent of the body's total mineral content. It is easily absorbed but barely stored -- about 90 percent of ingested potassium is excreted in the urine -- so Wallach states a significant daily intake of 5,000 milligrams is required. Chronic potassium deficiency shows as muscular weakness and mental apathy, and its most serious event is hypokalemic (low-potassium) cardiac failure. Diuretics (both natural and prescribed), sweating from colds, flu or exercise, vomiting and diarrhea all increase the loss of potassium and other minerals.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000096.claim_text: Wallach presents lithium as an essential trace mineral for mental and behavioral health, not merely a pharmaceutical. He states that in humans, clinical depression, manic depression, 'bi-polar' disease and autism are hallmarks of lithium deficiency, and that hyperactivity, attention-deficit disorder (ADD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) belong to the same picture. Although psychiatrists describe depression and manic depression as rooted in negative feelings and self-recrimination, Wallach notes they nonetheless treat it successfully with the trace mineral lithium -- which to him shows the conditions are fundamentally a lithium deficiency, aggravated by high sugar or alcohol intake. He reports that the risk of clinical depression has nearly doubled with each generation since 1915 and that its age of onset keeps dropping. As supporting evidence he cites Dr. Gerhard Schrauzer (University of California, San Diego), whose study of 27 Texas counties (1978-1987) found that areas whose drinking water contained little or no lithium had significantly higher rates of suicide, homicide and drug-related arrests than counties with water-lithium levels of 70 to 170 micrograms per liter. He adds that normal individuals carry roughly 400 times more lithium in their hair than violent criminals do, that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) estimates a daily lithium intake of 650 to 3,100 micrograms (much of it metallic and poorly absorbed), and that lithium supplementation shifts serum vitamin B12 levels.

autism are hallmarks of Li deficiency

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000098.claim_text: Magnesium is essential to all living organisms, second only to potassium as an intracellular cation; the adult body holds 20 to 28 grams, about 60% of it in bone. It powers energy production and protein synthesis, muscle contractility and nerve excitability, is a cofactor for countless enzymes, and is a constituent of chlorophyll. Calcium and magnesium play antagonistic roles in muscle -- calcium the stimulator, magnesium the relaxer -- so an excess of calcium can induce magnesium-deficiency signs, and an excess of magnesium inhibits bone calcification. Wallach lists a wide range of magnesium-deficiency diseases and symptoms: asthma, anorexia, menstrual migraines, growth failure, electrocardiogram (ECG) changes, neuromuscular problems, tetany and convulsions, depression, muscular weakness, muscle tics, tremors, vertigo, and calcification of the small arteries and soft tissue. Absorption ranges from about 24% for metallic sources to 85% for plant-derived colloidal sources; fat, phytates and calcium reduce it while vitamin D has no effect. He notes there is no evidence of toxicity up to 6,000 milligrams per day when the kidneys are healthy.

WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000099.claim_text: Manganese is essential to all known living organisms; it activates numerous enzyme systems (including those for glucose metabolism, energy production and the antioxidant superoxide dismutase) and is a constituent of many metalloenzymes, hormones and proteins. Wallach stresses its role in building the fragile ear bones and joint cartilage. He describes the deficiency diseases as very striking, ranging from severe congenital birth defects -- congenital ataxia, congenital deafness, chondromalacia, chondrodystrophy and 'slipped tendon' -- to asthma, convulsions, retarded growth, skeletal defects, infertility (failure to ovulate, testicular atrophy), stillbirths/miscarriages, loss of libido, and defects of chondroitin-sulfate metabolism that show up as joint problems: temporomandibular joint disorder (TMJ), repetitive motion syndrome and carpal tunnel syndrome. He argues most carpal tunnel and repetitive-motion cases are really manganese deficiency, not a purely mechanical injury. Separately, an EXCESS of manganese (from some water supplies or industrial exposure) can instead produce a Parkinson-like syndrome or a schizophrenia-like psychiatric disorder ('locura manganica').

Wallach states that classic protein (nitrogen) deficiency results in infertility, poor growth, lowered immune status, edema, and Kwashiorkor -- the potbellied, thin children of third-world countries. Sodium-chloride deficiency arises mainly in hot weather or heavy exercise with profuse sweating; Wallach warns that 'water intoxication' killed infants fed low-sodium formulas -- their brains swelled from a simple sodium deficiency -- and that the treatment for sodium deficiency is water and salt, taken orally or as 0.9% intravenous saline.

WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000004.claim_text: Wallach's prescribed solution: osteoporosis of the skull and spine (Wallach's Fibrous Dysplasia) is preventable and reversible by supplementing the full set of 90 essential nutrients -- 60 minerals, 16 vitamins, 12 amino acids, and 3 fatty acids -- dosed for bodyweight, and by protecting absorption through avoiding 'bad foods' and gluten (wheat, barley, rye, oats). In his words: "Osteoporosis of the skull and spine, Wallach's Fibrous Dysplasia, are preventable, amenable, and reversible with supplementation with the 90 essential nutrients, 60 minerals, 16 vitamins, 12 amino acids, and 3 fatty acids appropriate for bodyweight. Absorption is essential and so avoiding the bad foods AND gluten (wheat, barley, rye, oats) is imperative to get maximum benefit."
WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000004.verbatim:
Osteoporosis of the skull and spine, Wallach’s Fibrous Dysplasia, are
preventable, amenable, and reversible with supplementation with the 90
essential nutrients, 60 minerals, 16 vitamins, 12 amino acids, and 3 fatty acids
appropriate for bodyweight. Absorption is essential and so avoiding the bad
foods AND gluten (wheat, barley, rye, oats) is imperative to get maximum
benefit.

WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000005.claim_text: Wallach explains that the olfactory (first cranial) nerve carries the sense of smell from the lining of the nose through the cribriform plate of the skull to the brain. When osteoporosis of the skull narrows that bony channel, the nerve is pinched and the sense of smell is reduced or lost entirely (anosmia). In his words: "The olfactory nerve originates in the nasal mucosa and travels through the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to the olfactory lobe of the brain to produce the sense of smell. Osteoporosis of the skull will reduce the caliber of the tunnels resulting in the reduction of or the total loss of the sense of smell."
WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000005.verbatim:
The olfactory nerve originates in the nasal mucosa and travels through the
cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to the olfactory lobe of the brain to
produce the sense of smell. Osteoporosis of the skull will reduce the caliber of
the tunnels resulting in the reduction of or the total loss of the sense of smell.

WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000006.claim_text: Wallach teaches that the optic (second cranial) nerve carries vision from the retina through the optic canal of the skull to the brain. Skull osteoporosis narrows that canal and pinches the nerve, causing optic nerve atrophy -- a gradual vision loss that eyeglasses (lens prescriptions) cannot correct. In his words: "Osteoporosis of the skull causes a reduction of the internal caliber of the optic canal resulting in optic nerve atrophy (ONA) which produces a gradual vision loss that will not benefit from lens prescriptions."
WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000006.verbatim:
Osteoporosis of the skull causes a reduction of the internal caliber of the
optic canal resulting in optic nerve atrophy (ONA) which produces a gradual
vision loss that will not benefit from lens prescriptions.

WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000007.claim_text: Wallach maps the oculomotor (third cranial) nerve, which controls the pupil's response to light and four of the six eye muscles -- including the elevator palpebrae that lifts the upper eyelid. When skull osteoporosis pinches this nerve (per his disease table) the result is ptosis (a drooping eyelid) and a pupil that no longer responds to light. In his words: "This nerve travels through the eye via the superior orbital fissure to activate the eye muscles elevator palpebrae, superior rectus, medial rectus and inferior rectus motor muscles."
WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000007.verbatim:
This nerve travels through the eye via

the superior orbital fissure to activate the eye muscles elevator palpebrae, superior rectus, medial rectus and inferior rectus motor muscles.

WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000008.claim_text: Wallach describes the trochlear (fourth cranial) nerve as the motor nerve of the superior oblique muscle, which controls downward, outward and inward eye movement. When skull osteoporosis pinches it (per his disease table) the eyes no longer move together, producing double vision (diplopia), palsy, and pain above the eyebrow. In his words: "The trochlear nerve is a motor nerve that travels through the superior orbital fissure. This nerve enervates the somatomotor muscle and the superior oblique muscle that controls the superior oblique muscle which controls the downward, outward and inward eye movement."
WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000008.verbatim:
The trochlear nerve is a motor nerve that travels through the superior
orbital fissure. This nerve enervates the somatomotor muscle and the superior
oblique muscle that controls the superior oblique muscle which controls the
downward, outward and inward eye movement.

WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000009.claim_text: Wallach identifies the trigeminal (fifth cranial) nerve -- the largest cranial nerve, carrying sensation from the face and motor control of the jaw -- as the source of classic trigeminal neuralgia when osteoporosis of the skull strangles (pinches) it. This reframes trigeminal neuralgia as a nutritional/structural problem rather than an idiopathic one. In his words: "Strangulation of the trigeminal nerve is secondary to osteoporosis of the skull which produces the classic trigeminal neuralgia."
WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000009.verbatim:
Strangulation of the trigeminal nerve is secondary to osteoporosis of the
skull which produces the classic trigeminal neuralgia.

WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000010.claim_text: Wallach explains the abducens (sixth cranial) nerve controls the lateral rectus muscle that turns the eye outward. When it is squeezed in the superior orbital fissure (by skull osteoporosis) it produces an 'eye palsy' in which the eyes cross inward toward the nose -- strabismus. In his words: "This nerve originates in the pons region of the brain stem then enters the eye socket where it controls the lateral rectus muscle. When squeezed as it travels through the superior orbital fissure it produces an “eye palsy” where the eyes cross inward toward the nose."

This nerve originates in the
pons region of the brain stem then enters the eye socket where it controls the
lateral rectus muscle. When squeezed as it travels through the superior orbital

fissure it produces an “eye palsy” where the eyes cross inward toward the nose.

WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000011.claim_text: Wallach attributes Bell's palsy (facial paralysis) to strangulation of the facial (seventh cranial) nerve as it passes through bony tunnels narrowed by skull osteoporosis (Paget's Disease / Wallach's Fibrous Dysplasia), which he says produces many forms of neuralgia including the classic Bell's palsy. In his words: "Strangulation of the facial nerves as it passes through the obstructed tunnels (Paget's Disease / Wallach's Fibrous Dysplasia) produces many forms of neuralgia including the classic Bell's palsy."
WAL-CLM-IAIYH-000011.verbatim:
